blocks.text: Where McKinney Sits on the North Dallas Price Curve

McKinney is a growth market with a split personality. Downtown Historic McKinney is a grid of brick storefronts converted into law offices, agencies, and boutique professional suites, many with original hardwood and narrow stairs. Craig Ranch and the Eldorado corridor, by contrast, are filled with newer suburban office parks, medical office buildings, and corporate regional centers with LVT, carpet tile, and big surface parking lots. Both segments share one pricing reality: labor in McKinney runs slightly cheaper than in Frisco or Plano, which is why our index assigns a 0.96x cost multiplier.

Contract hourly rates in McKinney fall at $34-$58, against a national standard band of $35-$65. The reference median janitor wage is about $15.84 per hour. That 4% discount compounds on larger contracts: a 25,000 sq ft regional office cleaned nightly saves roughly $1,000-$2,000 per month compared with an identical building priced at the national benchmark. For a small downtown suite, though, the per-visit minimum of $90-$135 erases most of the discount, so smaller tenants should compare value through scope and frequency rather than rate alone.
McKinney Cost Index by Office Size

These ranges apply national size-bracket rates times 0.96, assume commercial carpet with a 1.0 flooring factor, and use 4.33 weeks per month. Restrooms, breakrooms, and glass are excluded so you can compare base scope apples to apples.

blocks.text: The spread inside each row reflects scope density and building condition. A Craig Ranch office with open-plan carpet, two restrooms, and few private offices lands near the low end. A downtown suite with hardwood, many small rooms, and a stair landing tends to price at the top because cleaners lose productivity moving between rooms and switching tools.
Spring Pollen and Commuter Traffic: The Hidden Floor Cost

Collin County spring pollen, especially oak in March and April, arrives as a fine yellow film tracked through every entry. Combined with heavy commuter foot traffic from surrounding subdivisions, it grinds into carpet traffic lanes and dulls LVT finish faster than in a downtown tower with covered parking. Buyers who ignore this see carpet that looks gray by summer and request an unplanned extraction at premium pricing.

blocks.title: Budget the pollen season in advance
blocks.text: Add a quarterly deep floor program at about $0.03-$0.06 per sq ft per month (roughly $144-$288 per month for 5,000 sq ft at the 0.96x multiplier) and schedule one extraction in early May, right after peak pollen. Ask for an increased walk-off mat rotation from March through May as a seasonal line item.

blocks.text: COI and Bonding Expectations in North Dallas Suburbs

Property managers across McKinney's office parks follow the same playbook as the broader North Dallas suburbs: they want proof of commercial general liability, workers' compensation, and a janitorial bond or third-party crime policy before a vendor receives keys. A bond protects you if a vendor employee steals equipment or data. It is different from liability insurance, which covers property damage and injuries. Many small operators carry liability but skip bonding, so it is a fast filter during vendor screening.

items: Request the COI directly from the vendor's insurance agent with your company and landlord named as certificate holders and additional insureds.
Confirm the janitorial bond or crime policy covers third-party property, not just the vendor's own losses.
Ask whether staff pass background checks before receiving keys or alarm codes, particularly for medical offices along the Eldorado corridor.
Verify OSHA Hazard Communication training, chemical labeling, and Safety Data Sheet access; request bloodborne pathogens training records for restroom staff.
If you want certified low-toxicity chemistry, specify Green Seal GS-37 or equivalent products in the scope rather than relying on a 'green cleaning' marketing claim.

blocks.text: Matching Tools to Downtown Hardwood and Suburban LVT

Tool choice affects both quality and labor hours. Wide open lobbies in Craig Ranch are fastest with a 36-inch cotton dust mop on a 360-degree swivel frame and 60-inch handle, which captures pollen and grit before any damp mopping. Historic downtown hardwood calls for a wood-safe system such as an 18-inch aluminum flat mop with washable microfiber dusting and wet pads, which limits water exposure that can cup old boards. For high-touch points such as door levers, desk edges, and shared phones, a refillable 700-count bucket of EPA List N disinfecting wipes speeds the work, provided the cleaner keeps surfaces visibly wet for the labeled contact time.

items.name: Pick a frequency by headcount
items.text: Under 15 occupants usually suits 1x-2x weekly; 15 to 60 suits 3x weekly; above that, consider nightly service.

items.name: Request three bids on identical scope
items.text: Give every vendor the same written scope, restroom count, and floor plan so the numbers are comparable.

items.name: Check math against 4.33 weeks
items.text: Weekly visits times 4.33 equals monthly visits. A vendor quoting 4 visits per month for weekly service is under-billing and may short you visits later.

items.name: Add seasonal floor care
items.text: Schedule extraction or scrub-and-recoat after spring pollen rather than waiting for complaints.

items.name: Write in a 30-day out clause
items.text: Keep a termination-for-convenience clause so you can switch vendors without penalty if quality slips.

faqs.q: Is office cleaning cheaper in McKinney than in Frisco or Plano?
faqs.a: Slightly. McKinney carries a 0.96x multiplier versus 1.0x for Frisco, so identical scope costs about 4% less. On a 10,000 sq ft office cleaned three times weekly, that is the difference between roughly $8,299-$14,227 per month in McKinney and $8,645-$14,820 in Frisco.

faqs.q: How is weekly cleaning converted to a monthly price?
faqs.a: Multiply visits per week by 4.33 weeks per month. Weekly service equals 4.33 visits per month, twice weekly equals 8.66, and five nights weekly equals 21.65. Multiply that by the per-visit price, then add monthly items such as an amortized deep floor program.

faqs.q: What does a janitorial bond cover for a McKinney business?
faqs.a: A janitorial bond or crime policy reimburses you if a vendor's employee steals property, cash, or equipment from your office. It is separate from general liability insurance, which covers accidental damage and injuries. Ask for both, and make sure the bond covers client property.

faqs.q: Should a McKinney medical office pay more for cleaning?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Exam rooms and patient restrooms require EPA-registered disinfectants used at full dwell time, bloodborne pathogen trained staff, and often sharps handling protocols. Expect medical suites to price toward the top of the range or use hourly specialty rates of about $55-$95 nationally.

faqs.q: What is typically excluded from McKinney office cleaning quotes?
faqs.a: Carpet extraction, hard floor strip-and-wax, exterior windows, blinds, high dusting, and post-renovation cleanup are commonly excluded. Ask each vendor to list exclusions in writing so a lower bid is not simply a thinner scope.
